item.title: Jennifer Aniston, boyfriend Jim Curtis’ chemistry shines as she reveals ‘deep fear’ during interview
item.description: Jennifer Aniston interviewed boyfriend Jim Curtis about "The Book of Possibility" at the 92nd Street Y, revealing a deep fear of public speaking.
item.content:encoded:
Jennifer Aniston and boyfriend Jim Curtis’ chemistry was on full display Wednesday evening when the "Friends" star interviewed the wellness coach about his new book.

While the 57-year-old kept it professional as she questioned him about his life and how he came to write his self-help guide, "The Book of Possibility," their connection was undeniable.

The "Friends" star later revealed that she was overcoming a "very deep, deep fear of public speaking" by interviewing him.

"You’d never know it," Curtis told her.

'FRIENDS' STARS JENNIFER ANISTON AND COURTENEY COX SOAK UP THE SUN DURING MALLORCA YACHT GETAWAY

The actress started out the 30-minute interview by reminiscing about how she used to go to gym class in the building where they were sitting, the 92nd Street Y in New York City, and play dodgeball, which wasn’t her favorite thing, since she wasn’t "sporty."

"So, it was me just knowing that I was going to go into — it was dodgeball, the huge red balls — and I’d just walk into the room, and there’s no, like, yard. It’s a building, so you just have to run for dear life, cover for dear life. Stand as far back into a corner as you possibly can. So, it’s quite a full-circle moment to be back here with you, speaking of dodging balls."

PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE

She continued to laughter, "So, I’m so excited to be here talking about ‘The Book of Possibility.’ Have I completely embarrassed you?"

"No, not yet. We’re still on track here," he laughed. "First question, please."

5 WAYS TO STAY FIT AND HEALTHY WHILE NAVIGATING MAJOR LIFE CHANGES: 'REALLY POWERFUL'

Aniston prefaced her first question by saying, "I know a lot about you," then asked the transformational coach about his journey to becoming the person he is now.

While discussing his earlier work on Wall Street carrying boxes around the New York Stock Exchange, Curtis said he began to feel accepted by the coworkers who would tease him by yelling "Run, Forrest, Run!" a reference to "Forrest Gump."

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

"It was the first time that I ever felt really accepted, because if they were making fun of me, I was truly accepted."

"Really?" she asked.

"Yes, please don’t adopt that," he replied. 

BRAT PACK ICON ANDREW MCCARTHY SAYS DRINKING 'DERAILED MY CAREER ENTIRELY'

Later, Curtis became emotional while discussing his "ultimate low" when he was in a hospital in severe pain struggling to get a diagnosis that made him realize "it’s time to change." Aniston also became emotional and teared up.

"What a beautiful story," she said, having to clear her throat. "Thank you so much for sharing that. And, also, you reached this point where you’re met with two roads, and you definitely went with the road less traveled in your case."

At the end of the interview, Curtis praised Aniston for her "fantastic" questions, adding that they "kind of" went over them before but not too much.

"I didn’t ask you one question that was prepared," the actress deadpanned. "I don’t know what you’re talking about."

JUST 5 MINUTES OF PRAYER COULD HAVE SURPRISING HEALTH BENEFITS, STUDY FINDS

After the interview, Curtis surprised Aniston by springing some questions on her from the audience. 

"Just relax, these won’t be very painful," he teased.

Once Aniston answered the questions about the possibilities she’s choosing, her best advice and how she handles stress — "Deep breaths and meditation" — the couple stood and hugged and shared a chaste kiss.

JENNIFER ANISTON REACTS TO EX-HUSBAND JUSTIN THEROUX'S BABY ANNOUNCEMENT

After Aniston left the stage, Curtis urged the audience to take "reckless abandon" and cheer for her as loudly as they could so she would consider taking part in another event.

The couple, who have been linked for over a year now, often keep their relationship private, although they have opened up about it in the past.

And the star shared a recent photo dump on Instagram of her summer that included a photo of her blowing a kiss to the camera with Curtis in the background.

item.title: Cavaliers star Donovan Mitchell reveals how booze helped fuel his legendary 71-point game
item.description: Donovan Mitchell revealed on the "Cousins" podcast that a few New Year's drinks preceded his historic 71-point game against the Chicago Bulls.
item.content:encoded:
There are certain sports where I think it’s widely believed, if not accepted as a cold, hard fact, that alcohol can improve performance.

Hasn't everyone's golf game improved with a little swing oil?

However, I didn't think basketball was one of the sports, at least not until Cleveland Cavaliers star Donovan Mitchell revealed that he dropped a cool 71 points back in 2023 with a little help from grandpa's old cough medicine.

AMERICAN TENNIS STAR AMANDA ANISIMOVA LEAVES FANS CONVINCED SHE DRANK BEER MID-MATCH WITH MYSTERY BEVERAGE

Back on January 2, 2023, Mitchell and the Cavs took on the Chicago Bulls.

The two teams ended up in an overtime thriller that the Cavs won 145-134, with Mitchell dropping a career-high 71 in the process.

"We played them on New Year’s Eve," Mitchell recalled on the "Cousins" podcast hosted by NBA greats Vince Carter and Tracy McGrady. "Then we had New Year’s in Cleveland. Then we played the next day. Now I will say this. I’ve never drank before a game in my life. It was New Year’s. So I did have a drink — a few drinks — the night before the game."

NO SEX FOR 10 WEEKS? CHAMPIONSHIP TEAM'S PLAYOFF STRATEGY RAISES EYEBROWS

Hey, many a beer leaguer has done that very thing. In fact, like I said, certain sports benefit from a few pops. Bowling is one, perhaps darts.

Hell, I've always argued that part of playing cornhole well is having a beer in your hand for balance.

"Never done that in my career," Mitchell said. "Haven’t done it since. So I tell people like that was probably what, you know, allowed me to have the night I had."

Mitchell is a professional because if that had happened to most of us, we would’ve thought, "Wait, if a few drinks equal 71 points, then it only makes sense that after many drinks I could be holding up a piece of paper with '100' written on it after the game."

Of course, that's not usually how it works...

...or is it?

item.title: Will Ospreay's era as AEW champion begins, learns he'll have title defense at All Out: 'I am the standard now'
item.description: Will Ospreay declared himself "the Billy goat" on "Dynamite" before his first AEW World Championship defense was set against Jon Moxley.
item.content:encoded:
Will Ospreay found out quickly who his first All Elite Wrestling (AEW) World Championship title defense was going to be against.

The "Aerial Assassin" started AEW "Dynamite" on Wednesday with an impassioned promo, calling his All In opponent Kenny Omega "the best wrestler in the world" for the last 10 years and "still is."

COMPLETE PRO WRESTLING COVERAGE ON OUTKICK

"I think about the people that have held this belt before," he said. "Chris Jericho, ‘Hangman’ Page, Jon Moxley, Kenny Omega, Bryan Danielson, Swerve Strickland … and I have to pinch myself a little bit. These guys were once-upon-a-time my heroes. I would watch them on TV. … These guys are my heroes and now the reality is, I’m amongst all of them. I worked hard for this, mate. All my idols, they’re now my rivals.

"I’m one of these guys that struggle to be able to say that I’m the guy. I haven’t got that much confidence in me. But then I look down at this belt and you can all look at it through your screens, bruv, I am the standard now. I am the Billy goat. I am the best in the world. I am your AEW world champion. And if anyone is going to take it from me, you’re going to need to walk through the same fire that I went through and I will see you at the end of the line, bruv."

Ospreay was later thrust into a 10-man tag team match with Andrade El Idolo, Callum Newman, Francesco Akira and Henare against Gabe Kidd, Bishop Kaun, Ricochet, Toa Liona and Clark Connors. Ospreay’s team won but the beat down was on afterward.

Kidd was about to hit Ospreay with a chair when Moxley stepped into the ring to take it away from him. Technically, Kidd and Connors are aligned with Moxley’s faction, The Death Riders. But Moxley has clearly shown he has a soft spot for Ospreay. Moxley helped Ospreay strengthen his body after he recovered from a neck injury. He also handed Ospreay the Union Jack before Ospreay stepped onto the stage at All In.

As Moxley stared down Ospreay, he handed him his world title back. The crowd then got ramped into a frenzy. The video board featured what was coming next for Ospreay and Moxley.

A match at All Out on Sept. 26 for the AEW World Championship.

Andrade has a guaranteed title shot lined up as well, though it’s unclear when he will embark on that journey. Andrade won the Casino Gauntlet match to earn the right for a title match.

For now, Ospreay and Moxley will battle it out at the end of the month.

item.title: Stephen A Smith warns Hasan Piker will ‘contaminate’ Democrats in the midterms, ‘come back to haunt them’
item.description: Stephen A. Smith warns that Hasan Piker's growing political influence could haunt Democrats in general elections and hand Republicans a weapon.
item.content:encoded:
ESPN personality Stephen A. Smith warned Thursday that far-left streamer Hasan Piker could become a general election liability for Democrats, telling Politico host Dasha Burns during "The Conversation with Dasha Burns" that Piker's influence could hurt the party beyond its progressive base and give Republicans ammunition against candidates who embrace him.

Smith said he believed Piker’s growing political footprint would ultimately hurt Democrats.

"It's a negative because I think, over the long haul, from a general populist perspective, it's going to contaminate the electorate on the left side of the aisle," he said. "It's going to come back to haunt them."

HASAN PIKER IS BECOMING THE 'FACE OF THE PROGRESSIVE MOVEMENT,' FORMER DEMOCRATIC OPERATIVE WARNS

The Republican National Committee (RNC) has already sought to turn Piker's relationship with Democratic candidates into a broader indictment of the party. RNC national press secretary Natalie Baldassarre told Fox News Digital in August that Democrats were refusing to confront Piker's influence as Michigan Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed faced scrutiny over campaigning with the streamer.

"El-Sayed is a terrorist sympathizer and an America-hating socialist," Baldassarre said. "His refusal to distance himself from Hamas-hugging radicals like Hasan Piker reaffirms his true allegiance is to terrorist groups, not America.

"Democrats' refusal to disavow this clown shows they either share his poisonous ideology or they're too cowardly to confront it."

Smith's warnings came as Piker's role in Democratic politics has become an issue in one of the country's most consequential Senate races. A recent Fox News poll of Michigan registered voters found Republican nominee Mike Rogers leading El-Sayed 51% to 47%, within the margin of sampling error. While 98% of self-described Democratic Socialists of America supporters backed El-Sayed, his support dropped to 69% among non-DSA Democrats and independents.

PIKER DEMANDS DEMOCRATS DEFEND HIM FROM ATTACKS, CLAIMS HE’S NO ‘TOXIC RADICAL FORCE'

El-Sayed previously explained directly to Smith why he has resisted pressure to disavow Piker, who has supported him and appeared alongside him during the campaign.

"What I'm saying is there are 3 million people who listen to Hasan," El-Sayed said. "I want to offer them a pathway into an electoral movement where, rather than sit outside of the electoral system, they see a pathway around the things that they agree with that he says that I agree with and a pathway that disavows the things that I disagree with. And, so, it's important."

Smith summarized El-Sayed's strategy as an effort to win over Piker's audience rather than an endorsement of the streamer personally.

"So, you're not thinking about him. You’re not thinking about him. You’re thinking about the 3 million people that support him, and you're trying to get those votes. That's what you're saying?" Smith said.

HASAN PIKER INSISTS ABDUL EL-SAYED ASKED HIM TO 'STUMP' FOR MICHIGAN CAMPAIGN AMID BACKLASH

El-Sayed confirmed Smith’s characterization. 

"Exactly," he said.

Fox News Digital reported last week that El-Sayed attempted to put distance between his campaign and Piker after the streamer faced backlash over comments about American Jews and Israel. Piker endorsed El-Sayed and appeared at multiple campaign events, including his primary night gathering.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

Piker has faced years of controversy over political rhetoric, including his 2019 declaration that "America deserved 9/11," which he later retracted, and more recent remarks involving Israel and American Jews.

Fox News Digital reached out to Piker, the DNC and the RNC for comment but did not immediately receive responses.

item.title: California girls’ sports advocates vow fight after judge tosses trans athlete case: 'Far from over'
item.description: The Justice Department is weighing an appeal after a federal judge dismissed Trump's lawsuit over transgender athletes in California girls' sports.
item.content:encoded:
Advocates for girls' sports vowed to keep fighting after a federal judge dismissed a Department of Justice lawsuit  challenging California policies that allow biological male athletes to compete on girls' school sports teams.

A DOJ spokesperson told Fox News Digital the administration remains committed to enforcing President Donald Trump’s policy barring biological males from girls’ sports despite the setback and is considering an appeal.

"We are disappointed by the Court’s order, and remain committed to enforcing President Trump’s agenda preventing boys from playing in girls’ sports," the spokesperson said. "We are evaluating our options for appeal."

Sophia Lorey, California Family Council outreach director and a former college soccer player who organized "Save Girls' Sports" demonstrations in California, told Fox News Digital that the ruling did not resolve what she called the central Title IX dispute.

NEWSOM FACES CRITICISM FOR STATE'S STANCE ON TRANS ATHLETES IN GIRLS' SPORTS AFTER SCOTUS RULING

"California should not mistake a courtroom technicality for a victory," she said. "The judge did not rule that allowing males into girls’ sports is fair, lawful, or consistent with Title IX. This case was dismissed on a technical issue without ever deciding the fundamental question at the heart of this fight."

The court avoided the underlying debate over biological fairness entirely. Instead, U.S. District Judge Cynthia Valenzuela grounded her decision in administrative funding rules, finding that the federal government failed to give California explicit prior notice before threatening to pull $44 billion in education funds. 

The Justice Department sued the California Department of Education (CADOE) and California Interscholastic Federation (CIF) in July 2025, alleging their transgender athlete policies discriminated against female athletes.

"I hope to see this decision appealed, but regardless, this fight is far from over," Lorey continued. "California lawmakers have the power right now to protect female athletes. A courtroom technicality does not erase biological sex, and it does not make discrimination against girls acceptable. We will not stop until CA girls are protected…California girls are still paying the price, losing medals, opportunities, roster spots, and privacy while state leaders prioritize gender identity over biological reality."

NEWSOM'S OFFICE RESPONDS TO SCOTUS RULING ON WOMEN'S SPORTS AS CALIFORNIA FACES ONGOING TRANS ATHLETE WAVE

Sonja Shaw, a candidate for California superintendent of public instruction who has been involved in filing federal civil rights complaints over transgender athlete policies, also sharply criticized the dismissal.

"Parents in California are no strangers to this fight, or to these underhanded tactics. We stood up to Gavin Newsom and the CIF when they decided girls’ sports and girls’ locker rooms were political fodder," she said. "A Biden-appointed judge just tossed out a case that should have protected female athletes, and she did it after the Supreme Court already ruled that states can keep women’s teams as a safe space for biological females. That is a political choice dressed up as law, and it is the girls who get robbed."

"This fight is not going away, and neither am I," Shaw continued. "I am not backing down because an activist judge in a kangaroo court dismissed a case. This is a hill we are willing to die on. We will keep fighting for fairness, safety, privacy and the future of female athletes. California parents have been told 'no' before, and we refused to quit then. We’re not quitting now. We will keep standing, we will keep fighting, and we will keep protecting our girls."

SUPREME COURT MAKES RULING ON TRANS ATHLETES IN WOMEN'S SPORTS

The California Interscholastic Federation declined to weigh in on the court’s dismissal when reached by Fox News Digital on Thursday.

"The CIF does not comment on legal matters," CIF Director of Media Rebecca Brutlag said.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

The California Department of Education also declined to address the substance of the ruling when reached by Fox News Digital on Thursday, citing the ongoing legal proceedings.

"The California Department of Education cannot comment on pending litigation," a CDE spokesperson said.

The legal fight intensified after transgender Jurupa Valley High School athlete AB Hernandez won girls’ events at California’s state track championships, prompting federal scrutiny and changes by the CIF intended to preserve qualifying and podium positions for biological female athletes.

Fox News Digital reached out to the White House for comment, but did not immediately receive a response.

OutKick's Alejandro Avila contributed to this report.

item.title: Marijuana users may face hidden driving danger that standard tests can miss
item.description: Cannabis edible users registered THC levels nearly 10 times lower than smokers despite similar driving impairment, exposing a potential road safety gap.
item.content:encoded:
A new study warns that driving after eating cannabis edibles can significantly impair road performance and reaction times, even if blood tests show THC levels far below the legal limit.

The findings, published in JAMA Network Open, highlight a potential challenge for impaired-driving enforcement in Canada and some U.S. jurisdictions.

Most previous cannabis-driving studies have involved smoked or inhaled marijuana, which more rapidly spikes levels of THC (tetrahydrocannabinol, the main psychoactive compound in cannabis) in the bloodstream.

AMERICA HITS MAJOR MARIJUANA MILESTONE AS DAILY WEED USE SURPASSES DAILY DRINKING

Edibles are absorbed more slowly and can produce driving impairment even when blood THC concentrations remain relatively low.

Researchers found that drivers who consumed higher doses of edible THC struggled with lane control, had slower reaction times and experienced greater speed fluctuations. Yet, their blood tests stayed below the standard legal cutoff used to prove impairment at roadside traffic stops.

To assess how oral cannabis impacts driving, researchers at the Centre for Addiction and Mental Health in Toronto conducted a trial with 40 healthy adult volunteers who regularly use cannabis.

Each participant attended four separate sessions in which they consumed soft-chew gummies containing either 0, 2, 10 or 20 milligrams of THC.

CANNABIS COMPOUNDS COULD REVERSE DISEASE AFFECTING ONE-THIRD OF ADULTS

The researchers then tested the drivers using a driving simulator at two, five and 24 hours after consumption, tracking how well drivers stayed in their lane, how quickly they reacted to road events and how consistently they maintained their speed.

Blood samples and self-reported ratings of intoxication were also collected.

The results showed driving impairment at two and five hours after consuming 10- and 20-milligram gummies. Compared with placebo, participants who consumed those doses had greater variability in lane position, while the 20-milligram dose was also linked to slower reaction times and less consistent speed control.

Participants also recognized their own limitations, reporting a lower willingness to drive and reduced confidence in their driving skills after taking the gummies.

The highest blood THC concentrations averaged 1.6 nanograms per milliliter after the 10-milligram dose and 3.4 nanograms per milliliter after the 20-milligram dose. Those levels were below the commonly used 5-ng/mL threshold, although THC limits vary by jurisdiction and some individual samples exceeded 5 ng/mL.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

By comparison, participants in the team’s previous smoked-cannabis study showed similar levels of impairment while reaching an average peak blood THC concentration of 30.3 nanograms per milliliter, nearly 10 times higher than the 20-milligram edible group.

The study did have some limitations. Tests were conducted on virtual simulators rather than actual roads, meaning drivers faced no real physical risk during the experiments. It also focused on regular cannabis users, so it is unclear how occasional users might react to similar doses.

Additionally, minimal residual effects were detected after 24 hours. While maximum speed remained slightly higher among participants on the 10-milligram and 20-milligram doses, subjective feelings of intoxication had completely faded.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

In an accompanying commentary, Dr. José Ignacio Nazif-Munoz of the Université de Sherbrooke noted that these biological differences pose a challenge for law enforcement.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

Because edibles are absorbed slowly through the digestive system, standard blood tests may fail to identify unsafe drivers, leaving policymakers searching for more reliable roadside tools.

"The delayed absorption and prolonged duration of effects of edible cannabis distinguish it from smoked or inhaled cannabis, complicating the interpretation of biological measures," he wrote.

item.title: Iran prefers conflict with US over peace to suppress internal uprising, human rights activist warns
item.description: A human rights activist says Iran's regime fears its own population more than U.S. airstrikes, using Strait of Hormuz friction for survival.
item.content:encoded:
Regime leaders in Iran are more content to see continued confrontation with the United States and its Gulf neighbors rather than pursuing peace in an effort to keep their disenchanted population at bay, one expert says.

U.S. forces have launched airstrikes against Iran in recent days following a brief pause in hostilities amid renewed flare-ups in the Strait of Hormuz.

Tehran isn't as concerned about military action against the country, but rather discontent among Iranians, Dr. Majid Sadeghpour, a human rights activist and the political director of the Organization of Iranian-American Communities, told Fox News Digital.

TRUMP RETALIATES AFTER IRAN ATTACK AS EXPERT WARNS REGIME IS GROWING MORE DANGEROUS

Sadeghpour noted that U.S. officials offered guarantees to Tehran that provided a pathway to peace for Iran.

"You get America to give you a guarantee that it wouldn't seek regime change. Nevertheless, they still attacked ships afterward," Sadeghpour said. "They still attacked our bases in Jordan and Bahrain. So that speaks to the fact that the real threat to the regime is not the bombs from outside, but rather the population uprising."

INSIDE TEHRAN: IRANIANS DESCRIBE IRGC'S BRUTAL RULE, POVERTY — ASK TRUMP TO 'STAY THE COURSE'

"For a regime that's militarized and requires friction, its survival now depends on that friction," he added.

Iran has experienced major uprisings in recent years driven by economic collapse, high inflation, and deep discontent with the regime's strict religious interpretation of Islam. In addition, the Iranian government has suppressed anti-government riots and protests with deadly force and arbitrary arrests and detention, according to human rights observers.

The war with the U.S. helps the regime, Sadeghpour said, by refocusing the Iranian public's attention elsewhere.

Meanwhile, Iran has continued to target commercial ships in the strait in violation of an agreement not to do so, Vice President JD Vance said Thursday.

IRAN ACCELERATES EXECUTION CAMPAIGN AGAINST ANTI-REGIME ACTIVISTS AMID INTERNET CENSORSHIP

"The Iranians are doing what the Iranians do," Vance said. "I think that they're losing their capabilities by the day. I think they're realizing… that their control over the Strait of Hormuz is effectively gone, and it's a diminishing asset."

In order to effect regime change, the U.S. should focus its efforts on the Iranian population, said Sadeghpour, because Iranian leaders will likely drag out the conflict with the U.S. for as long as they can.

"The regime is thinking about the day, the hour after the exhausted population gets calm, and will immediately look around, 'how am I going to get rid of this regime? And who's going to help me do that?' And so that is what the regime is afraid of," he said.

TRUMP REVIVES IRAN REGIME CHANGE SPECULATION WITH CRYPTIC CALL FOR PEOPLE TO 'RISE UP'

Meanwhile, President Donald Trump on Wednesday said he isn't focused on bringing Tehran to the bargaining table, saying he "couldn't care less" if Iran signs a "worthless" agreement.

"They are just playing out the inevitable," Trump wrote on Truth Social. "When are the Iranian people going to rise up and fight?"

item.title: EXCLUSIVE: FBI extraditions soar as Patel ramps up foreign outreach, vows 'no sanctuary'
item.description: FBI Director Kash Patel says FBI extraditions of international fugitives to the United States are up 65%, with 157 executed amid a sweeping manhunt push.
item.content:encoded:
FIRST ON FOX: FBI Director Kash Patel has dramatically expanded direct outreach to foreign partners in an effort to bring international fugitives back to the United States.

FBI data exclusively obtained by Fox News Digital shows Patel made 100 calls to international partners in his first 18 months, compared with nine by his predecessor during the final 18 months of the Biden administration.

Compared to the last 18 months of the Biden administration, extraditions were up 65%, and FTOCs (foreign transfer of custody), in which a fugitive or suspect is apprehended overseas and transferred into U.S. custody, are up 54%, the FBI said.

In that time, the FBI has executed 157 extraditions and 86 FTOCs.

FBI BRINGS BACK FUGITIVE ACCUSED IN $3.7B MEDICARE FRAUD SCHEME AFTER CAPTURE IN TURKEY

"When I became FBI director, I made clear that we would relentlessly manhunt high‑value targets from overseas, and we’ve delivered," FBI Director Kash Patel told Fox News Digital. 

"It’s a direct result of President [Donald] Trump’s relationships with foreign governments, which allow us to work in spaces where we were never permitted to before and Attorney General Todd Blanche’s leadership giving us the legal tools we need to return these subjects back to America to face charges.

"These targets are literally the worst of the worst, and we will give them no sanctuary."

MAN ACCUSED OF KILLING WIFE ON WEDDING NIGHT BROUGHT BACK TO US AFTER YEARS ON THE RUN IN MEXICO

On Monday, a Honduran citizen on the FBI's 10 Most Wanted Fugitives list was extradited to Philadelphia after 25 years on the run for the alleged rape and murder of a 5-year-old girl, Fox News exclusively reported.

Alexis Flores was arrested in February, and Honduran authorities agreed to extradite him to the U.S. The FBI said Flores had been removed from the fugitives list in March 2025 due to the prior Honduran government’s refusal to extradite him for his offenses, citing local laws limiting extradition.

EXCLUSIVE: ALLEGED $32M COVID-19 FRAUD FUGITIVE CAPTURED IN JAMAICA AND RETURNED TO US, FBI SAYS

Since June, the FBI has conducted more than 70 extraditions, Patel said at the time of Flores' extradition to the U.S.

In March, Zobaidul Amin, a Bangladeshi national, was extradited from Malaysia to the U.S. to face charges related to one of the most prolific online child exploitation schemes.

Prosecutors allege Amin posed as a teenager on Instagram and Snapchat and coerced hundreds of minor victims — some as young as 11 — into producing sexually explicit images and videos. Authorities said he then threatened to share those images with friends, family and classmates unless the victims sent more.

Another recent example is the case of Abdullah Anwar, 28, a Texas resident who was brought back from Qatar to face fraud charges. Anwar fled the U.S. for Pakistan but was arrested in Qatar before authorities there agreed to extradite him to Texas.

FBI WRAPS UP CYBERCRIME OPERATION TARGETING GLOBAL NETWORKS PREYING ON AMERICANS

The FBI has prioritized the extradition of suspects and fugitives abroad. From 2022 to 2025, former FBI Director Christopher Wray made 20 calls to foreign partners, including nine in his last 18 months during the Biden administration, the agency said.

Patel has made 100 calls in his first 18 months, a 400% increase over those made during Wray's four years and a 1,011% call increase over Wray's final 18 months with the Biden administration.

Typically, the FBI works with foreign authorities and governments to track and arrest suspects hiding in other countries. Once someone is arrested, the Justice Department will formally request that person be handed over to U.S. custody using existing international treaties.

Once the foreign government approves the handover, FBI agents travel abroad, take physical custody of the fugitive and fly them back to the U.S. for trial.

item.title: Jeffries threatens 'serious response' after Democrats help GOP advance anti-socialism vote
item.description: Hakeem Jeffries threatened a "serious response" after Reps. Jared Golden and Marie Gluesenkamp Perez broke ranks on a key GOP procedural vote.
item.content:encoded:
House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., threatened Thursday to pursue a "serious response" against two Democratic lawmakers during an appearance on "The Don Lemon Show" after they broke ranks with their party and helped Republicans pass a procedural rule Tuesday that advanced an anti-socialism resolution and several other GOP-backed measures.

Jeffries said Democratic leadership considered the move by Reps. Jared Golden, D-Maine, and Marie Gluesenkamp Perez, D-Wash., serious enough to refer the matter to the House Democratic Caucus’ Committee on Caucus Rules for possible action.

"We indicated that it was a significant breach that requires a serious response," he said. "And we have referred the matter to the committee on caucus rules for further discussion and action."

HAKEEM JEFFRIES REJECTS MEDICARE FOR ALL, DSA AGENDA AS RO KHANNA CALLS HEALTH PLAN 'MOST IMPORTANT PRIORITY'

Golden’s office pushed back on the criticism in a statement to Fox News Digital, explaining that the Maine Democrat’s vote was aimed at advancing legislation important to his state’s lobster industry rather than helping Republicans politically.

"The Congressman’s vote on the rule was about advancing a critical bill for his district, the Northeast Lobstermen Protection Act," Communications Director Mario Moretto said. "And he’s been clear about that in conversations with his colleagues in the House."

Fox News Digital reached out to Jeffries and the DNC for comment, but did not receive an immediate response.

MIKE JOHNSON TAUNTS HAKEEM JEFFRIES FOR LOSING DEMS' CIVIL WAR 'IN HIS OWN BACKYARD'

The official House roll call showed the rule, H. Res. 1499, passed 210-208, with 207 Republicans, Golden, Gluesenkamp Perez and one independent voting in favor. Five Republicans opposed the rule, meaning the measure would have failed in a tie without the two Democratic votes. The rule authorized consideration of H.R. 9436, Golden's Northeast Lobstermen Protection Act, along with the resolution condemning socialism and other legislation.

Golden’s bill later passed the House 219-196. The legislation would extend until 2035 a moratorium on certain new regulations intended to protect the endangered North Atlantic right whale. Golden’s office said the regulations could threaten Maine’s lobster industry, while additional time would allow regulators to collect better data.

Golden celebrated the bill's passage in a statement Tuesday and emphasized his willingness to work across party lines.

TOP DEM TORCHES SOCIALISTS TAKING OVER HIS PARTY: 'THEY'RE ANTI-AMERICAN'

"This bill is a big win not only for fishermen in Maine, but for bipartisanship in Congress," he said. "While the threat of unnecessary, industry-killing regulations is a matter of survival for lobster harvesters in Maine, the issues at play affect fishermen across the Northeast."

Jeffries' threat came after Democratic leaders had already condemned Golden and Gluesenkamp Perez in a joint statement Tuesday, accusing the pair of blindsiding the caucus on a procedural vote that had been on the verge of failing. Jeffries, House Minority Whip Katherine Clark, D-Mass., and House Democratic Caucus Chair Pete Aguilar, D-Calif., asked the caucus rules committee to take up the matter "in short order."

Gluesenkamp Perez also defended her decision in a statement following the vote, provided to Fox News Digital by her office Thursday, framing it around legislation affecting working waterfronts and arguing policymakers should listen to the people whose livelihoods depend on natural resources.

"Working people need a seat at the table and electeds need to listen to them, not data from the 1990s," Gluesenkamp Perez said.

item.title: Kamala Harris says she 'supports' Dems who don't want her on campaign trail: 'Whatever they need to do to win'
item.description: Red state Democrats are reportedly urging former Vice President Kamala Harris to stay far away from their 2026 midterm races, and Harris responded.
item.content:encoded:
MS NOW’s Peter Alexander confronted former Vice President Kamala Harris Thursday to respond to reporting that red state Democrats are asking her to stay far away from their midterm races.

Alexander showed a Politico headline on screen to Harris that read, "Kamala Harris is wading into the midterms. Red state Dems want her to stay away," before asking if she could respond to the report.

"Politico reports that you are wading into some of the midterms and that red state, not blue or purple state, but red state Democrats in states that Donald Trump won are encouraging you to stay away for fear it could impact their races there. Your response to some of that reporting?"

IOWA DEM GUBERNATORIAL CANDIDATE SAYS HE WOULD NOT WANT BIDEN OR HARRIS TO CAMPAIGN FOR HIM

Harris replied, "Listen, Peter, we need to win, OK? Bottom line, we need to win. I have run locally, I’ve run for statewide office and, obviously, nationally. And these candidates know what they need to do to win, and I would expect nothing less. 

"I look forward to being on the trail and helping folks where I can be helpful, but we have got to put a check on this lawless administration and deliver what Americans need and deserve. Lower costs, affordable healthcare, affordable childcare, you name it. So, I support them in doing whatever they need to do to win."

When asked whether she would be on the trail as a presidential candidate in 2028, Harris replied, "I’m focused on ’26," adding, "’28 doesn’t matter if we don’t win ’26.'"

According to Politico, "Iowa’s two most prominent Democratic candidates have said they do not want Harris to campaign for them. Alaska’s Democratic Senate nominee rejected a fundraising solicitation Harris sent on her behalf. And a swing-district Democrat in Wisconsin and a long-shot Senate hopeful in Kansas both told Politico they would prefer Harris keep her distance."

The article quoted one local Democratic candidate in another state who has made a noticeable rhetorical pivot from past politics to appease working-class conservative voters.

"I received 9,000 more votes than Harris in 2024," said Democrat Rebecca Cooke, who is running against Republican Rep. Derrick Van Orden in western Wisconsin. "I don’t need anyone to come and campaign with me in my district. I do the work of building relationships — including across the aisle — on my own."

DEMOCRATS TARGETING 12 ADDITIONAL RED DISTRICTS IN MIDTERMS PUSH TO RETAKE HOUSE

Democratic consultant Julian Epstein suggested the Democrats still remain a divided party in comments to Fox News Digital.

"The problem with postmodern Democrats is that they lack self-awareness, especially when it comes to swing voters needed to win most elections," Epstein said. 

"Moderate Democrats don't want Kamala because they think she's an empty suit who can't answer tough questions. They also think she's way too far left. When confronted, Democrats have this reflex of deflecting, saying what's really important is doubling down on a bloated welfare state, the same welfare state expansionism that failed us during the Biden years."

Former RNC national spokesperson Elizabeth Pipko said Harris' less-than-stellar history is an indictment of her party's lack of leadership.

"It’s a sad state of affairs when the former vice president is asked to remain off of the campaign trail because so many Democrats believe her record and unpopularity will hurt their chances in their own races. Harris’ answer was extremely weak and awkward considering she is now publicly both toying with the idea of running for president again and being rejected by members of her own party," she said.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

"We can’t forget that when Kamala Harris did in fact run for president, and her fate was left in the hands of the voters, she ended up dropping out of the 2020 Democratic primary before a single vote was cast," she added further. 

"Kamala Harris was never chosen by the American public to represent them nationally. She was picked by Joe Biden in 2020 after he committed to picking a woman as his vice president. And then she was handed the top of the ticket again when Biden dropped out before the 2024 election. Not only does she carry that baggage, but she knows that the American people have continuously rejected her.

"All of this also highlights the lack of leadership in the Democrat party today. Considering Biden’s age and health, she should be the obvious choice to lead the party, and yet it seems Democrats want to avoid that at all costs."

item.title: Washington female wrestler appeals Title IX case over alleged assault by trans opponent to Ninth Circuit
item.description: A Washington high school wrestler's Title IX case heads to the Ninth Circuit after she was allegedly assaulted by a trans competitor on the mat.
item.content:encoded:
A Washington high school athlete has taken her Title IX lawsuit to the Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals, seeking emergency safety protections before the upcoming wrestling season after she was allegedly sexually assaulted on the mat by a trans competitor last winter.

The teenager at the center of the lawsuit, previously identified by OutKick as Kallie Keeler, is referred to in court as K.M.K.

FEDERAL JUDGE DISMISSES DOJ LAWSUIT CHALLENGING CALIFORNIA POLICY ALLOWING BIOLOGICAL MALES IN GIRLS’ SPORTS

Alliance Defending Freedom announced Thursday, exclusively to OutKick, that it filed an emergency motion on behalf of K.M.K. and her mother, Stephanie Brown. The filing asks the appeals court to act by Sept. 25 and challenge policies enforced by the Washington Interscholastic Activities Association (WIAA), the Office of Superintendent of Public Instruction and the Puyallup School District.

After Brown and K.M.K. asked the court to protect her from another matchup against a biological male, U.S. District Judge David Castillo denied their request for a preliminary injunction on Aug. 23.

Brown and K.M.K. appealed on Aug. 25 and asked Castillo to protect K.M.K. while the appeal moved forward. When he denied that request on Aug. 31, ADF took the case to the Ninth Circuit.

LEADER OF FIRM THAT WON SCOTUS WOMEN'S SPORTS CASES OPENS UP ON DEALING WITH LIBERAL MEDIA, TITLE IX LAWSUITS

The case dates back to a South Puget Sound League tournament match on Dec. 6, 2025, at Emerald Ridge High School involving Rogers High School. K.M.K. took the mat without being told that her opponent was a biological male who identifies as trans.

During the match, the male competitor allegedly shoved his fingers through K.M.K.’s clothing and penetrated her genital area for several seconds. The complaint alleges K.M.K. allowed herself to be pinned to escape the encounter.

K.M.K. and her mother say they were never told before the match that she would face a trans competitor. They argue that Washington officials have left the door open to trans participation in girls’ high school athletics while keeping female athletes and their parents in the dark about potential safety risks.

The family says the school’s response after the match deepened its concerns.

DOJ LAWSUIT TARGETS ALLEGED SCHOOL ‘SECRET GENDER TRANSITIONS’ POLICIES THAT KEEP PARENTS IN THE DARK

Brown first alerted Rogers wrestling coach Lucia Scott on Dec. 8, two days after the match. She provided video evidence and asked the school to address what had happened. Scott allegedly forwarded the report to athletic director Peter Collins, who then involved principal Jason Smith.

"From that point, I kind of took the lead in talking to the coaches, and I made sure to send them an email and let them know what happened and ask them to kind of handle the situation," Brown previously told OutKick. "They assured me they were looking into it. They assured me it was gonna be handled. They passed it off to all these people, and then we just never heard anything else about it, like nothing further about it until we started pressing them."

The family alleges that school administrators waited 55 days to report the matter to authorities. According to the complaint, Smith notified a school resource officer on Jan. 30, 2026, while the district formally reported the matter to state child-welfare authorities on Feb. 12.

Brown also told OutKick that the coach initially said officials did not know a biological male was in the bracket.

ADALEIA CROSS PROMPTS VIRAL CONVERSATIONS WITH NEW CLAIMS IN SCOTUS TRANS ATHLETE SEXUAL HARASSMENT SCANDAL

"The reaction was that the coach said that they didn’t know that there was a biological male in the bracket," Brown said. "They said they would never have put her on the mat had they known, because she said she wouldn’t have put any of her athletes in that position."

Brown also alleges Smith initially responded to the incident by saying, "That’s wrestling."

Brown said the family ultimately filed the lawsuit because officials failed to respond properly to her daughter’s report.

"The decision to file the lawsuit was because the schools didn’t take our report of what happened to her seriously," Brown told OutKick. "They didn’t do anything to investigate it, correct it. They didn’t even keep in contact with me."

THE STATES THAT STILL ALLOW TRANS ATHLETES IN WOMEN'S SPORTS FACE QUESTIONS AFTER SUPREME COURT RULING

A subsequent district investigation allegedly acknowledged that the opponent likely touched K.M.K.’s private parts with force, causing her discomfort. But when Castillo denied the preliminary injunction, he did not describe the incident as an assault.

Instead, he ruled that the family had not shown K.M.K. faced a sufficiently likely risk of being harmed again under the legal standard for emergency relief.

That ruling is now one of the main issues before the Ninth Circuit.

ADF argues that forcing K.M.K. to compete against biological males, or making her give up her season if she refuses, violates Brown’s constitutional parental rights under Mirabelli v. Bonta. The attorneys also argue that the policy denies K.M.K. equal athletic opportunity under Title IX.

The filing cites the Supreme Court’s ruling in West Virginia v. B.P.J., in which the justices recognized that biological differences can create particularly serious safety risks in girls’ contact sports and place female athletes at a competitive disadvantage.

Brown and ADF want the Ninth Circuit to prevent officials from forcing K.M.K. to wrestle a biological male. At minimum, Brown wants advance notice and the ability to remove her daughter from any such match.

The WIAA told OutKick it was unable to comment due to pending litigation.

OutKick reached out to the Washington Office of Superintendent of Public Instruction, Washington Superintendent Chris Reykdal and the Puyallup School District for comment on K.M.K.'s appeal.

OutKick did not hear back from the WIAA or the Washington Office of Superintendent of Public Instruction on initial comments made by K.M.K. and Brown in July.

The transgender athlete and the athlete’s family are not defendants.

The appeal comes as courts continue to fight over the future of Title IX and trans participation in school sports. Earlier this week, a federal judge dismissed the Trump administration’s lawsuit against California officials over policies that allow trans athletes to compete according to their gender identity.

The judge concluded that the federal government had not clearly notified California that excluding trans athletes from girls’ sports was a condition of receiving federal education funding. The Justice Department is considering an appeal.

The California case and the Washington appeal involve different legal questions, but both concern rules governing biological males in girls’ sports. ADF argues that the Washington case presents a more immediate safety concern because it involves a teenage athlete who allegedly suffered an invasive incident during a girls’ wrestling match and could face a similar matchup again.

Without emergency intervention before wrestling season begins, Brown and ADF say K.M.K. will be forced to choose between risking another matchup against a biological male and losing another season of the sport she has practiced since childhood.

item.title: Should Milwaukee Brewers rest Jacob Misiorowski ahead of the postseason after poor start in Chicago?
item.description: Jake Peavy says the Milwaukee Brewers must skip Jacob Misiorowski's starts now to keep their NL Cy Young favorite fresh for a World Series run.
item.content:encoded:
There's one runaway favorite to win the National League Cy Young Award, and it's Milwaukee Brewers star pitcher Jacob Misiorowski.

"The Miz," as he's commonly known, has delivered on all of his immense promise in 2026, and then some. While elite velocity has always been one of his strong suits, Misiorowski has added impressive command and control to his repertoire. After walking over four hitters per nine innings in 2025, he's lowered that number to just 2.26 in 2026. And his other numbers have improved dramatically as a result.

Just 84 hits allowed in 155 innings, good for a minuscule 0.79 WHIP, with 227 strikeouts and a microscopic .154 batting average allowed. He's turning opposing major league hitters into pitchers hitting. No surprise then, that "The Miz" went 25 straight starts without allowing more than three earned runs.

BREWERS ACE JACOB MISIOROWSKI UNLOADS ON ANGEL STADIUM MOUND AFTER EMBARRASSING ANGELS LOSS

That streak ended Wednesday night. Matched up against the Chicago Cubs at Wrigley, Misiorowski turned in an uncharacteristically rough outing. He lasted just four innings, surrendering five runs on five hits and four walks while striking out five. The line was far from catastrophic, but it fell well short of the standard he has set for himself this season.

It continued a bit of a "concerning" pattern for the Brewers, where Misiorowski's otherworldly numbers have dropped off a bit in his most recent four starts.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

While his average fastball velocity remained at or above his season averages on Wednesday, the four innings added to his already career high total. In 2025, between the minors and big leagues, Misiorowski threw 129.1 innings. With at least four more starts remaining, he could push 180 for the year. And with the Brewers already a lock for the postseason and running away with the top overall seed, it's given rise to questions about the most advisable course of action for the 24-year-old.

One former Cy Young Award winner had a pretty definitive view on it: start skipping starts now.

BREWERS' JACKSON CHOURIO ENTERS LEGENDARY TERRITORY AS HE BLASTS 20TH HOME RUN OF 2026 SEASON

"In my career, once I started leaking oil, it was hard for me to even take a week or two off and get what I had back, if it was over usage," said former Padres star Jake Peavy during a discussion on MLB Now.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

"They've got to skip him a start or two and get him feeling fresh again," Peavy added. "If he's fresh, they can win the World Series...to win a World Series, you have to ride this guy.

If they're going to make the run they're making, it's going to have to be on the back of Misiorowski. Not to put too much on the young man, but this is just how you win. You've got to get him healthy, rested, let's go."

To his point, the Brewers might be considered the most likely team to win the World Series, given the advantages of a first-round bye and likely home field throughout the postseason. Their offense has been remarkably consistent, led by Jackson Chourio, Brice Turang, William Contreras, Andrew Vaughn and a surprising Jake Bauers. The starting staff is deep and talented, with Kyle Harrison and Logan Henderson a difficult matchup for any team in a short series. And the bullpen, with Trevor Megill, Abner Uribe, and the versatile Aaron Ashby shortening games.

But the key to finally winning the organization's first championship is, without question, Misiorowski. Few pitchers, if any, have been as reliably dominant as "The Miz" in 2026. The question then becomes: Is it worth sacrificing a few starts down the stretch if it means having him pitch three times in a best-of-seven NLCS or fill the kind of role Yoshinobu Yamamoto did for the Dodgers in the 2025 World Series?

Or do you value keeping him in his routine, and trust that he won't wear down as he approaches 200 innings between the regular and postseason? That's a question the Brewers coaching staff, front office, and likely Misiorowski himself are wrestling with right now, and the World Series might hinge on it.

item.title: Akron Zips vs. Wake Forest Demon Deacons week 1 college football pick favors under 48.5
item.description: College football week 1 features Akron Zips and Wake Forest Demon Deacons breaking in new quarterbacks and transfer portal additions in their opener.
item.content:encoded:
Week 1 of College Football is finally here. I’d call it the opening week of football, but we did get games last week, which were pretty entertaining. I’m trying to temper my expectations a bit as we have only one ranked matchup this week, and that doesn’t come until Sunday. Week 1 is set up for teams to try to beat the crap out of other teams so that they can get things in line before their conference schedule starts and they have tougher opponents. This game likely will be no different as Akron takes on Wake Forest.

Akron is not going to be a very good team this season, and is predicted to have about five wins. The Zips' over/under for the year is listed at 4.5 games and slightly juiced to the over. Their schedule doesn’t look like they have an overly difficult path, but there just isn’t a ton of talent on the roster. Ben Finley, their quarterback from last season, is gone, and they turn the ball over to Reese Poffenbarger.

It could be a good thing, though, going to Poffenbarger. He came over from Miami and North Texas, two schools that have had very dynamic offenses. However, he wasn’t the starter at either college. Jordan Gant is back in the backfield and had a decent year last year with a 4.8 yards-per-carry average. He only found the end zone six times, though. I have a bit of a mixed opinion on the Zips, as they have four transfers starting in their defensive unit. That could be good, but it might take a while for continuity and cohesion to come out for them.

SEC LAWYERS, LANE KIFFIN AND DEATH VALLEY: COLLEGE FOOTBALL’S WEEK 1 IS SET FOR FIREWORKS

Wake Forest is one of those schools that occasionally has a good season, but never really has a fully dominant team. They really aren’t expected to be much better than Akron, but they will be at least a little better. They are expected to have at least six wins this year. They have a tough schedule this year with Purdue next week and Miami the following week. It won’t be easy for them, but there are definitely a few winnable games (including this one) on the agenda.

Like Akron, the team has a new quarterback under center. Gio Lopez will be the primary thrower for them. He had a decent season last year at North Carolina, where he threw for 1,747 yards and 10 touchdowns. He did have five interceptions with it, though, so protecting the ball will be important for him. There has been a lot of change on this roster with two new offensive line members and two wide receivers coming in the transfer portal.

Usually when a team starts the season, they start rather slowly. When a team has transfers and revamps everything, I think they will start even slower. Both of these teams have a lot of changes and are learning new offenses in live action for the first time. I think the under 48.5 is the right look in this game. The Zips and Demon Deacons both have new quarterbacks, and neither is overly impressive. Give me the under 48.5.

item.title: Enes Kanter Freedom files lawsuit against Sky following ejection, ban after altercation with Natasha Cloud
item.description: Enes Kanter Freedom has filed a federal complaint against the Chicago Sky and more after his ejection following an altercation with guard Natasha Cloud on Aug. 23.
item.content:encoded:
Enes Kanter Freedom is taking legal action against the Chicago Sky following his ejection from Wintrust Arena following an altercation with guard Natasha Cloud during a game against the Indiana Fever. 

Freedom filed his federal complaint in U.S. District Court, where he said he was "peacefully exercising my First Amendment rights" by sitting near the baseline and wearing a T-shirt that read, "WOMAN noun, adult human female." Freedom was banned indefinitely from Wintrust Arena by the Sky, and he said he may be pursuing legal action because of it. 

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

Freedom’s lawsuit names Chicago Women’s Basketball Operations, LLC, which operates the Sky, the Metropolitan Pier and Exposition Authority (MPEA), which financed and built Wintrust Arena as a public project, and the City of Chicago as defendants, claiming they "combined and conspired, and acted jointly to execute their conspiracy, to discriminate against Plaintiff based on Plaintiff’s verbal and demonstrable expression of viewpoint and gender identity when they wrongfully ejected Plaintiff from a recent WNBA game."

"Defendants compounded and exacerbated Plaintiff’s injuries when they subsequently banned Plaintiff indefinitely from attendance," the lawsuit obtained by OutKick read. 

The lawsuit adds that Freedom "believes deeply and advocates forcefully that the integrity of women-only sports must be protected, and he has been explicit in many public appearances on this point." 

The suit also reiterates a point Freedom has made on numerous occasions, that he self-identifies as a player who is eligible to participate in the WNBA "because such declaration is all that is required by WNBA’s rules." Freedom has received backlash for his stance, which was also mentioned in the lawsuit. 

"Plaintiff has been the target of a torrent of hateful attacks and discriminatory actions based on Plaintiff’s viewpoint and gender identity," the lawsuit read. 

CHICAGO SKY OWNER OPENS UP ON ENES KANTER FREEDOM EJECTION, MAKES ANALOGY TO SHOOTING A GUN

The lawsuit proceeds to break down the events on Aug. 23 in the eyes of Freedom, which began with his manager sending a "courteous text message" to Sky GM Jeff Pagliocca, his old personal trainer, to inform him the former NBA center would be attending the game. Pagliocca allegedly responded, "Appreciate the text," but Sky owner Michael Alter allegedly alerted Wintrust Arena Security of Freedom’s expected attendance. 

It continues by saying Freedom was harassed by Sky fans, many of whom used vulgar language including, "Get your b---- a—out of Chicago, f--- you b----, b---- a-- n-----!," among others. 

"None of these fans were warned or ejected, despite profanity and racial slurs being express violations of the WNBA Fan Code of Conduct," the lawsuit read. 

During the third quarter of the game, Freedom stood and raised his arms in celebration of a three-pointer made by Sophie Cunningham, the Fever star who has also received vitriol for her stance on biological men participating in women’s sports. A few possessions later, Cloud made a shot, and following a timeout, she "initiated a vulgar, profanity-laced verbal tired directed at Plaintiff Freedom personally, and charged nearly half the length of the court toward where Plaintiff Freedom was sitting courtside," the lawsuit read. 

"Plaintiff Freedom believes that Cloud’s attack was motivated and triggered by the message on Plaintiff’s shirt and Plaintiff’s widely publicized viewpoint on protecting the integrity of women only sports," the lawsuit added. 

The lawsuit states that, while Freedom raised his arms "in confusion and disbelief," Cloud continued to scream out profanities in his direction "in violation of WNBA rules." Cloud was not ejected from the game, nor did the WNBA issue any disciplinary action. Alter also confirmed the Sky would not take action against Cloud. 

The lawsuit adds that Alter "subsequently mischaracterized the interaction" between Freedom and Cloud, claiming the former was "chirping" at her before the altercation. It also mentioned an interview Alter had with OutKick, where he likened what Freedom did to shooting a gun at someone. 

"I mean, to use an extreme example, when you shoot a gun at someone, you don’t get a warning, ‘Don’t do that again.’ Your action doesn’t deserve a warning. You take action that becomes a threat, you don’t get a warning," Alter told OutKick. 

Freedom claimed that damages against him continue "as long as the unconstitutional ban" from Wintrust Arena stays in effect. 

Freedom requested the court declare the defendants violated his First Amendment rights by ejecting him from Wintrust Arena and indefinitely barring him from re-entry as well as"an award of nominal and compensatory damages for Plaintiff’s losses incurred."

"My T-shirt did what the whole [WNBA] apparently couldn’t: define a woman," Kanter’s X post with his lawsuit read. "No threats. No violence. Just biology. And somehow, that required a security escort. You don’t have to agree with my speech but you don’t get to silence me for it. I will not be intimidated. I will not be silenced. I will continue to stand for women and defend free speech." 

The Sky and MPEA did not immediately respond to a request for comment by OutKick regarding Kanter’s lawsuit. The City of Chicago doesn't comment on pending litigation, an official said.

item.title: Cleveland Browns reset under Todd Monken after trading Myles Garrett and parting with Stefanski
item.description: Todd Monken inherits a Cleveland Browns roster in flux, with Deshaun Watson battling Shedeur Sanders and Dillon Gabriel for long-term snaps.
item.content:encoded:
With former Georgia and Ravens offensive architect Todd Monken stepping in as head coach following the departure of Kevin Stefanski, and Deshaun Watson competing alongside rookies Shedeur Sanders and Dillon Gabriel, Cleveland is aiming to reset its culture and rebuild its foundation in a brutal division.

The Browns endured a painful 2025 campaign, finishing dead last in the AFC North with a 5–12 record. Cleveland leaned on tight, low-scoring defensive scraps to pull out occasional victories, but those moments were few and far between. Their offense was inconsistent, but that should be expected considering they had three different quarterbacks. The team averaged a league-worst 16.4 points per game as passing inconsistencies, poor offensive line play, and a lack of rhythm derailed drives before they could start. The inability to move the chains or protect the quarterback eventually brought an end to Stefanski's six-year run in Cleveland, setting off a massive winter teardown.

The headlining blockbuster occurred when Cleveland traded two-time Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett to the Rams for a haul that included pass rusher Jared Verse and draft capital. It actually was a good trade for the Browns, getting capital and a talented player to at least somewhat replace Garrett.

BROWNS GENERAL MANAGER EXPLAINS WHY HE CHANGED HIS MIND ON TRADING MYLES GARRETT: 'OPPORTUNITY WAS TOO GREAT'

To jump-start the rebuild under Monken, the Browns overhauled their roster through free agency and draft weekend. They signed offensive line help in guard Zion Johnson and center Elgton Jenkins, added linebacker Quincy Williams and defensive tackle Kalia Davis, and stacked the offense with young skill talent like wide receiver Isaiah Bond and dynamic college running backs Quinshon Judkins and Dylan Sampson. They also drafted secondary depth and brought in veteran depth with pass rusher A.J. Epenesa and receiver Tylan Wallace.

Offensively, Monken inherited a revamped line, designed to open up lanes for a backfield rotation led by Judkins alongside veteran Jerry Jeudy and draft additions out wide. However, the quarterback room remains a massive wildcard as Watson attempts to fend off Shedeur Sanders and Dillon Gabriel for long-term snaps.

Garrett is not someone who could be replaced easily. While Verse and Alex Wright will man the edges and Denzel Ward remains an elite anchor in the secondary, the front seven lacks proven game-disrupting star power, leaving the defense reliant on scheme and discipline to hold up.

item.title: Dramatic video shows SWAT vehicle ramming tractor during tense Oregon standoff
item.description: Oregon man Erik Gordon Shunn allegedly fired more than 200 rounds, shot at a Clackamas County Sheriff’s Office drone and engaged in a standoff with a SWAT team.
item.content:encoded:
Video captured the dramatic moment a SWAT team rammed its vehicle into a tractor during a standoff with a suspect who allegedly went on a shooting spree near an Oregon home.

Erik Gordon Shunn, 53, reportedly targeted multiple tree workers Saturday afternoon south of Portland before confronting responding authorities, according to the Clackamas County Sheriff’s Office (CCSO). Officials said Shunn fired more than 200 rounds throughout the incident.

In a video captured by a CCSO drone, Shunn appeared to unleash a barrage of gunfire directly at the aircraft, according to authorities.

He later drove a compact tractor near the front of his home when a CCSO SWAT vehicle slammed into it, trapping the tractor against the house. Several SWAT personnel then jumped from the back of the vehicle and moved in to apprehend him.

VIDEO SHOWS POLICE TAKE DOWN COP KILLER WITH ARMORED VEHICLE AFTER GUNMAN TURNED NEIGHBORHOOD INTO WAR ZONE

According to officials, the Clackamas County SWAT Team responded to a report of an armed neighbor firing at professional arborists hired to cut down trees in a rural residential and farm area.

The 911 caller told dispatchers Shunn may have several guns, while witnesses estimated he fired roughly 20 rounds at tree company employees, officials said.

When authorities arrived, drones allegedly spotted Shunn in his driveway.

LOUISIANA MAN ACCUSED OF KILLING DEPUTY US MARSHAL FACES POSSIBLE DEATH PENALTY

He was "knocking down trees with a tractor in an apparent attempt to create a barricade," according to the CCSO.

Authorities said they ultimately decided to pin Shunn’s tractor after he became separated from his rifle while driving it near the front of the home.

"SWAT personnel used this window of opportunity because they believed it provided the highest likelihood of safely apprehending Shunn," CCSO officials said.

WATCH: MAN ACCUSED OF AIMING FLAMETHROWER AT OFFICERS SERVING EVICTION NOTICE IN WILD BODYCAM VIDEO

Shunn was treated before being taken to a local hospital for evaluation.

"First responders also checked on neighbors and tree workers to confirm their safety and evacuate them from the area," CCSO said.

No injuries were reported. Shunn’s mother, who was also at the home during the standoff, was also unharmed, according to the sheriff’s office.

Shunn was charged with second-degree attempted murder, first-degree attempted assault, recklessly endangering, unlawful use of a weapon, menacing, unlawful possession of firearms, first-degree attempted criminal mischief and interfering with a peace officer.

He is being held without bail at the Clackamas County Jail.

item.title: Smithsonian showdown intensifies as Trump administration issues a stark new warning
item.description: The Smithsonian Institution faces threats beyond its $1 billion federal funding as Trump administration claims evidence of antidiscrimination violations.
item.content:encoded:
The Trump administration says it has uncovered evidence that the Smithsonian Institution violated federal nondiscrimination laws and is threatening to withdraw support from its museums unless it corrects course, according to a letter recently made public by the Department of the Interior.

"The administration has recently uncovered evidence that the Smithsonian leadership's institutional culture may have resulted in significant violations of Federal antidiscrimination law, including creating a hostile work environment and engaging in practices that classify individuals and allocate opportunities, funding and other benefits on the basis of race, ethnicity and other protected characteristics," a letter sent jointly to the Smithsonian by the DOI and White House reads.

Specific evidence of illegal activity on the part of the Smithsonian was not included in the letter, and the DOI did not provide further information when reached for comment. A recent Fox News Digital investigation found that many leading figures at the Smithsonian, including those involved in hiring, have been strong proponents of diversity, equity and inclusion — something the Trump administration has previously framed as racially discriminatory.

TRUMP’S SMITHSONIAN CLASH EXPOSES STRIKING PATTERN AMONG MUSEUM CURATORS

Conservative political leaders, led by President Donald Trump, have accused the Smithsonian of allowing progressive ideology to shape its presentation of American history. An executive order signed in 2025 directed officials to remove what it called "improper ideology," from the museum.

"The Executive Order signed by the President of the United States clearly states ‘the Secretary of the Interior, the Director of the Office of Management and Budget, the Administrator of General Services, and the Assistant to the President for Domestic Policy shall identify and utilize any and all available authorities to promote the policy of this order and to restore trust in the Smithsonian Institution," a DOI spokesperson told Fox News Digital.

TRUMP TARGETS BIDEN-ERA BILLION-DOLLAR SMITHSONIAN BUDGETS AMID ANTI-'WOKE' PUSH

Liberals, meanwhile, have framed conservative criticism of the Smithsonian as a partisan attempt to influence the public presentation of history.

Unless the Smithsonian remedies the issues outlined in the DOI’s recent letter, as well as the general bias which conservatives allege exists at the institution, the administration says it will consider pulling support from it. The threats this time around, however, differ from the ongoing fight over the roughly $1 billion a year in federal funding the Smithsonian receives.

SMITHSONIAN'S TAXPAYER FUNDS FACE CHOPPING BLOCK AS GOP DEMANDS ACCOUNTABILITY FOR 'WOKE' HISTORY

"Those executive departments and agencies cannot in good conscience continue to support the Smithsonian under current leadership by, for example, loaning artifacts for exhibits, enabling procurement processes and making discretionary grants," the letter reads.

While the letter does not provide specific changes that the administration would like to see from the Smithsonian, it does note that an "appropriate response" from the organization "must likewise address executive leadership and institutional ideology."

That wording could be significant as the institution operates independently but is overseen by board members appointed by congressional resolutions that the president must sign into law. By October, there will be four openings on the institution’s board of regents, a fact the administration may leverage to increase its influence over the Smithsonian.

"Very few Americans want the Smithsonian National Museum of American History to be used, in the words of its director, as a ‘prime tool of social justice’ and as an instrument of ideological activism and advocacy,"  Vince Haley, the director of the White House's Domestic Policy Council told Fox News Digital when asked about the letter. "Unfortunately, the Saving America’s Story report demonstrates, using the statements of Museum leadership and the interpretive guidelines adopted by the Museum, that this is exactly what the Smithsonian’s flagship museum has become."

"During this 250th anniversary year of our heroic founding, the least our citizens are owed is an honest and inspiring account of American history. It should begin by telling the story of our Founding Fathers — who they were, what they did, and what they built. It is our hope and expectation that the Smithsonian will eventually rise once again to that noble obligation — to tell America’s story for our children, the world and future generations of Americans," he added.

WATCH: SMITHSONIAN HISTORY MUSEUM DIRECTOR STUMBLES OVER BASIC QUESTIONS ON SEX: ‘I’M NOT SURE’

DOI requests that representatives from the Smithsonian meet with administration officials "at [their] earliest convenience" to discuss the alleged bias and civil rights violations present at the institution.

"The museum does not take sides in America’s political debates. We preserve and document the evidence of American life in all of its breadth, so that the public can encounter the past and draw their own conclusions," National Museum of American History’s director Anthea Hartig said at a July congressional hearing.

The Smithsonian declined to comment on the letter when reached by Fox News Digital on Thursday.

Recent reporting has found that the museum’s leadership and many of its curators have backgrounds in liberal advocacy or Democratic politics. In addition to exhibits at the National Museum of American History, which the Trump administration characterized as demonizing America, even the Smithsonian-run National Zoo is inundated with information about DEI and gender equity.
